content: Write a public social post for our small stationery shop after its website was unavailable for three days during a sale. The outage ran from Friday at 9 a.m. to Monday at 9 a.m., all Eastern Time. A checkout update caused the failure; we do not have evidence of a security incident and should not speculate about one. The site is now working, but we cannot promise it will never fail again. Here is the actual compensation: the original 20% sitewide discount has been restored automatically from Monday at 9 a.m. through Thursday at 9 a.m. Eastern Time, giving shoppers a fresh 72 hours. No code is needed. It applies to merchandise, excludes shipping and gift cards, and cannot be combined with other discounts. We are not offering extra credits or free shipping. Some shoppers reported pending card authorizations without an order confirmation; support can check these through the site's Contact page, but we have not confirmed which became charges and cannot promise a refund date in this post. Write in a plain, accountable voice, own the disruption without blaming a supplier, explain the offer and its limits clearly, and give those with payment concerns a private next step. Do not ask people to post order or payment details publicly.

**We owe you an update.**

From Friday at 9 a.m. to Monday at 9 a.m. ET, our website was down during what was supposed to be a sale weekend. A checkout update we rolled out caused the failure. We don't believe this was a security incident, and we're not treating it as one.

The site is back up. We won't promise it will never happen again, but we're working to make sure it doesn't.

**The sale is back.** The original 20% sitewide discount has been restored automatically—no code needed. It runs from Monday at 9 a.m. through Thursday at 9 a.m. ET, giving you a fresh 72 hours to shop.

A few details so there's no confusion:

- Applies to merchandise only
- Excludes shipping and gift cards
- Cannot be combined with other discounts

We're not adding extra credits or free shipping on top of this. The restored discount is our way of making up for the lost time.

**If you tried to place an order during the outage** and saw a pending card authorization but never received an order confirmation: please reach out to us through the Contact page on our site. We can look into it for you. We haven't yet confirmed which of those authorizations became actual charges, so we don't want to make promises about refunds we can't keep right now—but we will check your specific situation.

Please don't post order numbers, payment details, or account information in the comments or replies. If you need help with a charge, the Contact page is the right place.

Thank you for your patience, and for sticking with a small shop even when things go sideways.

"We don't believe this was a security incident, and we're not treating it as one." 

Stop. This sounds like a legal disclaimer, not an apology. It’s defensive and creates a seed of doubt where there was none. A customer doesn't want to hear how you're "treating" an incident; they want an accountable admission of a technical failure. 

Rewrite that paragraph to be direct and humble without being evasive. How do you say this without sounding like a lawyer?

**We owe you an update.**

From Friday at 9 a.m. to Monday at 9 a.m. ET, our website was down during what was supposed to be a sale weekend. A checkout update we rolled out broke the site, and it stayed broken until we could fix it. That's on us.

The site is back up. We won't promise it will never happen again, but we're working to make sure it doesn't.

---

The fix is simple: name the cause and stop talking. "A checkout update we rolled out broke the site" is specific, honest, and doesn't invite the reader to wonder what else it might have been. The moment you say "it wasn't a security incident," you've put the idea in their head. Silence on that point is more reassuring than a denial.

The revised text is more direct. Now, clarify the compensation offer: Can you rephrase to specify that the 20% discount is valid on merchandise only, to avoid any potential misinterpretation that it applies to shipping or gift cards?

**The sale is back.** The original 20% discount on merchandise has been restored automatically—no code needed. It runs from Monday at 9 a.m. through Thursday at 9 a.m. ET, giving you a fresh 72 hours to shop.

A few details so there's no confusion:

- Shipping and gift cards are not included
- Cannot be combined with other discounts

---

The change is small but meaningful. Saying "20% discount on merchandise" up front means the reader already knows the scope before they reach the bullet points. The exclusions below now read as confirmation rather than a surprise, which reduces the chance someone adds a gift card to their cart and feels misled at checkout.
